content:
Hello, I am a new programmer (have like 7 months of coding experience), I've been trying to read a lot of kernel code to build understanding of the kernel and to learn. I can make sense of most of the code but I am unable to like connect it for some reason. I've also been trying to read patches (most of the time I am unable understand them... ).
I also tried sending a few patches (messed up pretty badly on those too... )
So, I wanted to ask am I trying to contribute to the kernel too early ?
Also, if someone could tell me how they started or share some learning resources I'll really be thankful.
Thanks.

7 months is indeed very early to tackle a huge, complex project like the kernel (all the more in Rust!). The prerequisite of a successful contribution is understanding what you are contributing to and how your contribution fits in the project. The kernel is also a bit of an outsider in the OSS world as patches are sent and reviewed the "old way" via email, which doesn't make things as simple as a Github pull request.

The first thing to understand is what you are interested in? Operating systems, Rust, anything else? Any experience in C (which is always useful to understand OS design)? The key to keeping motivation is having an itch to scratch, maintaining reasonable and incremental goals, and taking it easy.

Also nowadays anymore can fire a LLM to find something that appears broken and send a patch that addresses an issue, without really understanding it. Would that be fulfilling? I believe it is a good idea to get started with reasonable contributions that you can do without AI assistance, even if they seem trivial. You are more likely to hit the mark and increase your overall understanding that way.

I don't have experience in C beyond the basics as my first language was Rust and I've just been focusing on it till now. I'll start learning C properly too.

I am interested in driver design though I don't know how to get started in it. I've read a bit of CS:APP (learned the basics of C to read it.) and followed phillip opperman's guide to build a kernel in rust after which I've been just lost on how to progress anymore....

Also, I was generally trying to avoid using Ai as much as possible but as you probably already know, I did use it for the last patch I sent. I did write the first one by hand though (ended up breaking binder and tyr by it..). I'll try not to use it unless I am stuck from now as it's not fun unless I understand what's going on and what I am doing.

If it's not too much to ask, could you also share how you got into kernel development? It would help me a lot in figuring out how to get started.

Thanks for your guidance.
